title: The Empty Swing
hook: Every kid in my hometown knows the rule: if a swing is moving on its own, never push it.
lines: In the little town where I grew up, there's an old swing set in the park... and every kid there knows the rule.
If a swing is moving on its own... never push it.
My grandmother used to say it like a prayer. Because if you push it... it pushes back.
I moved away at eighteen. Last fall, after she died, I came home to empty out her house.
The shortcut from the store cuts right through that park.
One night, there was no wind at all... but the middle swing was moving.
Back... and forth. Back... and forth. A little higher every time.
Then, from the empty seat, a small voice whispered...
I didn't. I walked home fast, and I never looked back.
Around three a.m., a sound woke me. Grandma's porch swing... creaking.
I opened the front door. The porch swing was empty... and perfectly still.
Then two small, cold hands pressed flat against my back...
and a little voice said... my turn.
